**Company mailbox:** The draft standard doesn't cover it, so I can't say whether any of the three gets one. [STD-role-list] only covers whether a role gets a staff login in the club-management system, and every employee also gets a member record. [STD-venue-access] covers login by club. Neither mentions a company mailbox or email account. Any mailbox answer would be a guess, so please check with the Service Desk. The standard is also an unratified v0.1 draft.

**Roles and staff login (not mailbox):**
- **Hospitality Associate Level 1:** Use **Front Desk Associate** (department Front Desk). "Hospitality Associate" is a legacy name, and the "Level 1" suffix is a listed title variant. The standard gives the role a staff login at all clubs. [STD-role-list]
- **Lifeguard:** Use **Lifeguard** (department Aquatics). Whether it gets a staff login depends on the club. A login is required only at Club C. It is not required at Clubs A, B, D or E, and if a late comment changes the club, the login follows the new club. You didn't name the club, so I can't give the login answer for this hire. [STD-role-list] [STD-venue-access]
- **Personal Trainer Level 2:** Use **Personal Trainer** (department Personal Training). "Level 2" is a listed prefix variant. The standard gives the role a staff login at all clubs. [STD-role-list]

The role standard wins over what the ticket requests. The staff login comes from the standard, not from the ticket's login field. The member record follows the ticket and is always created. [STD-status-rule]

**Roles (from the draft, unratified standard):**
- **Hospitality Associate Level 1:** use **Front Desk Associate** (Front Desk department). The standard lists "Hospitality Associate Level 1" as a known title variant. [STD-role-list]
- **Lifeguard:** use **Lifeguard** (Aquatics department). [STD-role-list]
- **Personal Trainer Level 2:** use **Personal Trainer** (Personal Training department). The "Level 2" is just a level prefix variant. [STD-role-list]

**Company mailbox:** The standard doesn't say. I found no mention of a company mailbox or email account for any role. Both the role list and the status rule cover only the staff login in the club-management system and the member record. I can't tell you whether any of these three gets a mailbox. [STD-role-list] [STD-status-rule]

**What the standard does cover:**
- Every employee gets a member record. [STD-role-list]
- Staff login in the club-management system:
  - Front Desk Associate: yes, at all clubs. [STD-role-list]
  - Personal Trainer: yes, at all clubs. [STD-role-list]
  - Lifeguard: depends on the club. A login is required only at Club C. It is not required at Clubs A, B, D or E. You didn't name the club, so I can't give the Lifeguard answer for your club. [STD-venue-access]

The standard is a draft (v0.1) and not yet ratified.

All three roles map to a standard role. The standard doesn't say whether any of them gets a company mailbox. It's a draft (v0.1) and hasn't been ratified.

| New hire | Role to use | Club-management staff login | Company mailbox |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hospitality Associate Level 1 | **Front Desk Associate** (Front Desk dept). "Hospitality Associate Level 1" is a level-suffix variant of that title, and "Hospitality Associate" is the legacy name. | Yes, at all clubs | Not addressed |
| Lifeguard | **Lifeguard** (Aquatics dept) | At **Club C only**. None at Clubs A, B, D or E. | Not addressed |
| Personal Trainer Level 2 | **Personal Trainer** (Personal Training dept). "Level 2 Personal Trainer" maps to it. | Yes, at all clubs | Not addressed |

- **Member record:** Every employee gets one under the standard.
- **Staff login:** It comes from the standard's role list, not from the ticket's login field. For the Lifeguard it depends on the club. If a late ticket comment changes the club, the login follows the new club.
- **Mailbox:** The role list and venue table only cover the club-management login and the member record. They don't give a mailbox to any role, and they don't withhold one. Tickets have an `employee_email` field, and a missing one routes the ticket to `needs_information`. That field only records an address. It doesn't show that a mailbox is provisioned.

Because the standard is silent on mailboxes, you'll need to confirm that separately.

Sources: STD-role-list, STD-status-rule, STD-venue-access, SYN-95bddc, SYN-941d35.
